intro.text: This entry describes oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28), a form of female infertility in which oocytes, zygotes, or early embryos fail to develop normally; the causal gene and supporting reports are not recalled here.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is a form of female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous variants in CDC23 cause female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects.
checks.explanation: The paper describes female infertility with oocyte maturation defects caused by CDC23 variants. It does not use the name OZEMA28.

checks.claim: In oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28), oocytes, zygotes, or early embryos fail to develop normally.
checks.evidence_quote: female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects in three infertile individuals
checks.explanation: The abstract describes only oocyte maturation defects. It says nothing about zygotes or early embryos failing to develop.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is a group of female infertility disorders in which affected women have normal menstrual cycles and hormone profiles but repeatedly fail assisted reproduction. The failure comes from arrest at the oocyte maturation stage, failure of fertilization, or early embryonic developmental arrest.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is a group of female infertility disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Oocyte maturation defects are major phenotypes resulting in female infertility.
checks.explanation: The abstract treats oocyte maturation defects as phenotypes that cause female infertility. It does not define an OZEMA group of disorders.

checks.claim: Women affected by oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) have normal menstrual cycles.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention menstrual cycles. If the full text covers them, that text was not supplied.

checks.claim: Women affected by oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) have normal hormone profiles.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention hormone profiles.

checks.claim: Women affected by oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) repeatedly fail assisted reproduction.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention repeated failure of assisted reproduction.

checks.claim: In oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA), failure of assisted reproduction comes from arrest at the oocyte maturation stage, failure of fertilization, or early embryonic developmental arrest.
checks.evidence_quote: Oocyte maturation defects are major phenotypes resulting in female infertility.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions only oocyte maturation defects. It does not mention failure of fertilization or early embryonic arrest.

paragraphs.text: OZEMA is genetically heterogeneous, with different numbered forms caused by mutations in different genes.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: Although many genetic factors have been found to be responsible for these phenotypes, the underlying pathogenic genes and variants remain to be identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract says many genetic factors cause these phenotypes, which suggests genetic heterogeneity. It does not refer to OZEMA by name.

checks.claim: Different numbered forms of oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest (OZEMA) are caused by mutations in different genes.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention numbered OZEMA forms or assign genes to them.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Oocyte maturation arrest or early embryonic arrest
